newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGUESE POLICE PROBE BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGUESE POLICE PROBE BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: Portuguese police questioned a businessman on Wednesday over his allegations that he sought to bribe a referee on behalf of Porto soccer club 12 years ago.
Porto have fiercely denied the allegations and UEFA, European soccer's governing body, has sought an explanation from the Portuguese Football Association.
Hotel owner Fernando Barata was quizzed by police in the southern city of Faro where he lives, a police spokesman said.

Barata, a former chairman of the city's Farense soccer club, alleged earlier this week in television, radio and newspaper interviews that he had been asked by Porto to speak to the referee, a Romanian, ahead of Porto's European Cup Winners' Cup semifinal against Scottish club Aberdeen.
He said he had been asked to fix a 3-0 victory for Porto in the first leg but has not said how much money was offered. Porto won both the home and away legs 1-0.

Gilberto Madahil, chairman of the Portuguese Football Federation, said on Wednesday he had received a personal guarantee from Porto chairman Jorge Nino Pinto da Costa that there was "absolutely nothing" in the allegations.
Madahil said he had asked for a meeting with UEFA next Monday to deliver a personal report on the incident.
